title: Support health condition for container dependencies (--requires)
body:
### Feature request description

Environment
OS: CentOS Stream 10
Podman: 6.1.0
podman-compose: 1.5.0
Rootful Podman
Problem

Podman supports persistent container dependencies using --requires.

For example, podman-compose translates:

depends_on:
  db:
    condition: service_healthy

into:

podman create ... --requires=db ...

The dependency is stored by Podman:

"Dependencies": [
  "<db-container-id>"
]

However, the healthy condition is not stored.

As a result, after a reboot:

podman start --all

Podman starts the required container first, but does not wait for it to become healthy before starting the dependent container.

### Suggest potential solution

Suggestion

Could Podman support an optional condition for --requires, for example by storing additional dependency metadata?

Conceptually:

requires: db
condition: healthy

If the condition is missing, behavior remains exactly as today (started), so this should be backward compatible.

If the condition is healthy, podman start / podman start --all would:

start db
wait for db to become healthy
start dependent container

This would also allow Compose implementations to preserve depends_on: condition: service_healthy after the initial compose up.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

### Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

comments.body:
Hi @harryzz and maintainers!

I'd like to take this on. I did a code walkthrough of the creation, storage, and start paths and would love to validate the design with you before putting up a PR.

### 1. CLI & SpecGen Syntax
Extend `--requires` values with an optional `:condition` suffix, following the same colon-split precedent used in `--network name:ip=...` (`pkg/specgen/namespaces.go`):
* Syntax: `--requires <name>[:condition]`
* Supported conditions: `started` (default, preserves existing behavior) and `healthy`.
* Comma separation works out of the box with Cobra's `StringSliceVar`: `--requires db:healthy,cache:started`.
* Remote API / SpecGen: parse this in `specgenutil` and propagate to `SpecGenerator.DependencyContainers` (or dedicated dependency spec).

### 2. Storage & Backwards Compatibility (Additive)
To keep the SQLite relational integrity table (`ContainerDependency(ID, DependencyID)`) untouched and avoid breaking older container configs, preserve `ContainerConfig.Dependencies []string` (`libpod/container_config.go:81`) as-is for the dependency IDs.

Add a parallel field to `ContainerConfig`:
```go
// DependencyConditions maps a dependency container ID to the condition
// required before this container can start. Absent entries default to "started".
DependencyConditions map[string]string `json:"dependencyConditions,omitempty"`

Hi @i-OmSharma — thanks for picking this up!

Your `--requires db:healthy` syntax is a natural fit — it mirrors the Docker Compose V2 `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` convention directly at the Podman CLI level, which makes it the right direction for upstream.

For reference: I've already implemented and tested a working experimental version of this on CentOS Stream 10 aarch64 (two hosts, running in production). My approach was intentionally minimal — no CLI change — using a container label (`io.podman.compose.requires-healthy.v1`) set by patched podman-compose, with a new `libpod/container_dependency_health.go` reading it on start. No `ContainerConfig` or specgen changes, no DB migration.

That file might be useful as a reference when you implement the healthy-wait logic.

Happy to share the patches if they'd help.

Thanks for sharing the patch, @harryzz! 

The lock-handling pattern and the post-wait state verification (`dep.State() == Running`) to catch containers that exit immediately after reporting healthy are really solid edge-case catches. I'll make sure to incorporate those guardrails into the native `--requires` implementation.
